title: FTF inline style commands (bold/italic/underline/strikeout)
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Style Syntax")
text: FTF (Family Historian Text Format), the markup any live Notes/Text field is stored in, supports paired on/off inline style commands, freely nestable: bold ..., italic ..., underline ..., strikeout .... Example: 'An important point.' A run_lua script reading a Notes field with fhGetItemText sees this markup literally in the returned string — it is not stripped automatically. See run-lua-get-plain-text-from-richtext for how to get clean prose instead.

title: FTF font size and font commands
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Style Syntax")
text: Font size: <fs="+N"> / <fs="-N"> ... </fs> sets a relative point-size delta from the default — NOT additive/cumulative (nesting <fs="+3.5"> inside another <fs="+3.5"> does not make the inner text bigger than the outer). Font: <font="Name","Style",Charset> ... </font> takes up to 3 params — name (required), style (nil/roman/swiss/modern/script/decor/tech/bidi, default nil), charset (numeric: 0=ANSI, 1=default, 2=symbol — required for symbol fonts like Wingdings). To supply charset without style: <font="Wingdings",,2>.

title: FTF text colour and highlight commands
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Style Syntax")
text: Text colour: <clr="RRGGBB"> ... </clr> (default reverts to black), e.g. <clr="FF0000">red</clr>. Highlight (background) colour: <hl="RRGGBB"> ... </hl> (default reverts to white), e.g. <hl="FF0000">red background</hl>. Both take a single 6-hex-digit RGB string parameter, same format for both commands.

title: FTF paragraph-level formatting: bullet, indent, alignment
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Formatting Syntax")
text: Applies to a whole paragraph (or a table cell), only recognized at the very start of it. Bullet: paragraph starts with '*' (optionally followed by one space). Indent: paragraph starts with one or more '>' — the count is the indent depth. Alignment: <align=X> at the start, X is one of l/c/r/j (left/centre/right/justify; default left; justify has no visible effect on a table). When combined, the required order is indent, then alignment, then bullet-or-table (bullet and table are mutually exclusive) — e.g. '>>* This paragraph is indented twice and bulleted.' Indent/alignment can also apply to an entire table, not just a paragraph.

title: FTF table syntax
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Table Syntax")
text: A table can only start at the beginning of a line/paragraph (aside from a leading indent/alignment prefix) and cannot be nested inside another table in plain FTF (nesting is an eFTF-only, report-only feature). ... — one string parameter giving each column's width in twips (1/20 pt), separated by '|'; an omitted/empty width defaults to 800 twips, so means 2 columns, both default width. ... marks one row; cells inside are separated by '|' (escape a literal bar as '\|'). A single space immediately inside /before , and immediately either side of a '|', is trimmed and doesn't count as content. No text is allowed on the same line after — further text starts a new paragraph.

title: FTF web link syntax
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Web Link Syntax")
text: <web="URL"> inserts a link displayed as the URL itself; <web="URL","Display text"> supplies custom display text instead. Not clickable within a report, but may become so if the report is saved/exported as an HTML web page. This is plain textual markup — no companion table/index is involved, unlike record links and citations below.

title: FTF record link syntax (<rec=...>)
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Record Link Syntax")
text: <rec=Index,"DisplayText",Flag> marks an inline link to another record. Index is a position in a record-link table that FH stores internally alongside the rich text (created via the RichText object's AddRecordLink method — inserting the <rec=...> text directly does NOT create the underlying table entry). DisplayText is shown if the link is invalid/missing/deleted, or always if Flag is "text"; Flag is "auto" (display = the linked record's own, live-updating display name) or "text" (display = DisplayText always). Example: <rec=6,"Ian Stephen Munro",auto>. See ftf-record-links-and-citations-resolution for how to actually resolve Index to a record from run_lua.

title: FTF inline source citation marker syntax (<cit=...>)
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("FTF Source Citation Syntax")
text: <cit=Index> marks an inline citation reference within a block of rich text (e.g. 'the household was recorded here<cit=2>, but see also<cit=3>.'). Index is a position in a citation table FH stores internally alongside the rich text (created via the RichText object's AddCitation method — inserting the <cit=...> text directly does NOT create the underlying table entry). This is a different mechanism from a SOUR citation attached structurally to a Fact/Person/Family record — it's an inline marker embedded within a block of rich text instead. See ftf-record-links-and-citations-resolution for how to actually resolve Index to a citation from run_lua.

title: Resolving <rec=...>/<cit=...> markers from run_lua
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/Objects/rich_text/GetText.htm
text: fhGetItemText(ptr, "~") only ever returns the raw FTF string — a <rec=N,...>/<cit=N> marker in it is literal text, not something that call resolves for you. To actually resolve the markers, call fhGetValueAsRichText(ptr) to get a RichText object, then call its GetText method: `sText, bRich, tblRecLinks, tblCitLinks = rt:GetText()`. tblRecLinks/tblCitLinks are Lua tables (nil if the text has none) mapping a <rec=N,...>/<cit=N> marker's index N to an item pointer for the linked record/cited SOUR item — index N corresponds exactly to the marker's own first parameter, 1-based, no gaps. This is a live-API resolution path, distinct from (and not needing) whatever internal link-id mechanism a raw GEDCOM export uses to encode the same relationship on disk — that exported-file mechanism is out of scope for this bridge, see ADR 0003, since run_lua never reads or writes a .ged file directly.

title: FTF escaping rules
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/ftf_syntax.htm ("Special Characters in FTF Syntax")
text: Backslash (\) removes any special meaning from the character immediately following it, including escaping itself (\\ -> literal \). Characters with special meaning that need escaping when used literally: '<' (always — it starts a command; an unrecognized command is just silently ignored, not an error), '*' and '>' (only special at the very start of a paragraph), '|' (only special inside a table cell). A quoted command parameter is required if it contains a space, comma, '>', backslash, or double-quote; inside quotes, \" and \\ are the escaped forms of " and \. fhFtfEncode() escapes the FTF-special characters (\|<>*) in a string for you; fhFtfParamEncode() escapes just backslash/double-quote for a quoted command parameter.

title: Private text markers [[...]]
source: FH help: /help/fh8/privatenotes.html ("Private Notes")
text: Doubled square brackets mark a span of text as private, e.g. 'he limped as a result of a [[self-inflicted]] war wound' — can cover an entire note or just part of one. This is a separate mechanism from FTF's grammar (it can appear inside or outside an FTF-styled span, e.g. inside ...), handled as its own concern during parsing rather than as an FTF command. Works in any field that accepts multiple lines of text — Notes, Address, and the "Text from Source" field on Source/citation records — but NOT in single-line fields like "Where Within Source", even though double brackets can still be typed there (they just won't be treated as private). Private text is excluded from reports/books/GEDCOM exports by default, with separate options to include it and, if included, to strip the brackets themselves. From run_lua, RichText:GetPlainText(bIncPrivate, bRemBrackets) controls exactly this: bIncPrivate=false to drop private spans entirely, bRemBrackets=true to keep the text but strip the brackets.

title: Getting clean plain text out of a rich-text field
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/Objects/rich_text/GetPlainText.htm, /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/fhGetValueAsRichText.htm
text: fhGetItemText/fhGetValueAsText on a rich-text field (Notes, Source TEXT, citation DATA/TEXT, etc.) returns the raw FTF string, markup and all — e.g. a table shows up literally as ' apple | pear | orange ... ' rather than anything readable. To get clean prose instead: `rt = fhGetValueAsRichText(ptr)` then `sPlainText = rt:GetPlainText()` — strips all styling, tables, and links down to plain text (optional params bIncPrivate/bRemBrackets control private-text handling, see ftf-private-text-markers). Prefer GetPlainText over manually regexing out FTF commands when you just need a Note's readable content, e.g. to summarize it for the user.

title: FTF vs eFTF vs tFTF — which one run_lua actually sees
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/richtextsyntax.htm, /help/fh8plugins/api/eftf_syntax.htm, /help/fh8plugins/api/tftf_syntax.htm
text: Three related but distinct syntaxes. FTF is what's actually stored in any live rich-text field (Notes, Source TEXT, citation DATA/TEXT) — this is what run_lua reads and writes via GetText/SetText/AddText on a real record field. eFTF ("Enhanced FTF") is a superset used only when Family Historian itself constructs a report/book/website — never appears in a field run_lua reads, and if you write eFTF-only content into a real field via SetText, the features FTF doesn't support are silently dropped. tFTF is a text-only convenience variant of eFTF, usable only as an option to RichText:SetText(), whose sole difference from eFTF is its record-link syntax: <rec=QualifiedId,"DisplayText",Flag> using a qualified record id (e.g. "I67") instead of a record-link-table index — this lets a plugin add a record link as plain text without calling AddRecordLink. tFTF cannot express citations at all.

title: Shared Facts — and why FH's own help calls them Witnesses
source: FH help: /help/fh8/witnesses.html ("Witnesses"); underlying item shape per family_historian_mobile project's fh-tag-mapping-spec.md, verified there against real GEDCOM exports (Family Historian Sample Project 8, Mullins Family History) but not yet independently probed via a live run_lua call in this bridge
text: This project's own term for a Fact with participants beyond the record it's attached to is 'Shared Fact' (see CONTEXT.md) — but when reading FH's own help/UI, the same concept is called a 'Witness', and a fact that has one or more of them is called a 'Shared Event'; FH's help never uses the phrase 'Shared Fact' at all. Worth knowing when searching FH's own help corpus for this topic — search for 'witness', not 'shared fact'. Every fact (event or attribute) has one or two principals (the person(s) the fact is actually about); anyone else involved in a non-principal role (a minister, a bridesmaid, an executor, ...) is what FH calls a witness. Roles are free text, not a fixed enum — any number of participants can share the same role, and new roles can be invented freely. In the item tree run_lua already walks with MoveToFirstChildItem/MoveNext, each participant sits as a _SHAR child (points to an existing Individual) or _SHAN child (free-text name only, no Individual record exists) of the fact item, itself carrying a ROLE child holding the role's free text. Don't build logic that assumes a closed set of role strings.

title: Fact Flag vs Record Flag, and Rejected always beats Preferred
source: FH help: /help/fh8/howto_flagafact.html, /help/fh8/howto_recordflags.html; live-API mechanism: /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/fhGetFlagTag.htm
text: Two distinct flag mechanisms that happen to share some names and one implementation mechanism (fhGetFlagTag, a child '_FLGS' item). Record Flags mark an Individual record as a whole — only 2 built-in: Private, Living. Fact Flags mark one specific fact (Individual or Family) — 4 built-in: Private, Preferred, Tentative, Rejected. Both support unlimited custom flags via fhGetFlagTag(name, true[, bFactFlag]). A 'Private' record flag and a 'Private' fact flag are always distinct, even on the same person. Rejected always overrides Preferred: if a fact has both flags set, it is NOT treated as preferred — a Rejected fact is excluded from diagrams/reports/age-calculation regardless of what else is set on it. Where there's no Preferred fact of a given type (and none Rejected), FH treats the first-recorded one as the default.

title: Source Template fields vs Source Template definitions
source: FH help: /help/fh8/sourcesandsourcetemplates.html, /help/fh8/sourcetemplatefielddefinitiondialog.html
text: A Source Template field is one structured, populated value on a Source record or on a specific citation of it — e.g. a Registration District, a Date, a link to a Repository — created from a source template's field definition (name, code, type, prompt). Field types: Text, Name, Date, Place, Address, Repository (an optional link to a Repository record — unlike a plain generic Source record, which can link to at most one repository, a templated source can have any number of Repository-type fields), Enum, URL. This is distinct from the source template *definition* itself: reading/parsing the definition's own storage in detail is out of this bridge's scope (ADR 0003 — that ADR is about not modeling the exported-.ged wire format, not about the live API), but a citation's/source's own populated fields are ordinary child items in the same live item tree run_lua already walks: read them the same way as any custom fact (MoveToFirstChildItem/MoveNext), not via a fixed data-reference string, and don't assume every source has the same fields — which ones exist depends entirely on which template (if any) that particular source used. See source-template-creating-a-templated-source for how to create one (this is fully reachable live, not out of scope).

title: Creating a templated Source record and populating its fields via run_lua
source: FH plugin API help: /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/fhCreateItem.htm ("Metafields and Shortcuts", "Creating Source Records of Different Types"), /help/fh8plugins/api/DataStructure.htm, /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/fhSrcEnableAutoTitle.htm; live-verified against this project's own "Civil Registration Certificate" _SRCT template (record 50) — see issue thread creating source #41 for Nellie Record's 1895 birth certificate
text: A generic/free-form Source record (fhCreateItem("SOUR")) becomes a *templated* Source record purely by gaining a child item tagged `_SRCT` whose value links to an existing `_SRCT` template record: `local link = fhCreateItem("_SRCT", sourPtr); fhSetValueAsLink(link, templatePtr)`. This link must exist *before* creating any field values on the record — field creation fails otherwise. A `_SRCT` template record's own field *definitions* are child items tagged `FDEF` (not `_FIELD` — that tag is reserved for the value-holding metafields on the *Source* record itself, a different tag on a different record; don't conflate the two despite the similar '_FIELD'-adjacent naming), each with NAME/CODE/TYPE/PROM (prompt, only present for some types) subfields — walk these with MoveToFirstChildItem/MoveNext to discover a template's actual fields and their exact CODE strings, since these vary per-template and per-project. To populate a field value on the Source record, you cannot use fhCreateItem("_FIELD", sourPtr) directly (that tag can't be used to create a metafield) — instead pass a *shortcut* string as fhCreateItem's tag argument: `~PREFIX-CODE`, where PREFIX is a fixed 3-letter code for the field's TYPE (TX-Text, NM-Name, DT-Date, PL-Place, AD-Address, RP-Repository, EN-Enumeration, UL-URL) and CODE is exactly the field definition's own CODE value (e.g. `~EN-Type`, `~NM-Principal`, `~DT-Date`). If the shortcut doesn't match a field definition on the linked template, or the record isn't yet linked, fhCreateItem fails. Once created, set the metafield's value with the setter matching its underlying value kind, not its field type name: fhSetValueAsText for Text/Name/Place/Enum; fhSetValueAsDate(ptr, fhNewDate(iYear, iMonth, iDay)) for Date — fhNewDate takes numeric year/month/day arguments, NOT a date string; fhSetValueAsLink for Repository. After populating fields, call fhSrcEnableAutoTitle(sourPtr, true) to enable and refresh the record's title from the template's TITL format (a separate mini-language from Sentence Templates — see sentence-templates). A transcription/"Text from Source" is just the ordinary `TEXT` child tag on the Source record, populated the same way as any other rich-text field: `fhSetValueAsRichText(fhCreateItem("TEXT", sourPtr), fhNewRichText(transcriptionString, false))` (bRich=false so the transcription is stored as plain text, not parsed as FTF markup).

title: Sentence templates: the mini-language behind narrative-report sentences
source: FH help: /help/fh8/sentencetemplatecodes.html; live-API mechanism: /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/fhGetNarrSentenceTemplate.htm, /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/fhGetNarrSentence.htm
text: A Sentence Template is a small template-language string FH stores on a fact, used to render it as a natural-language sentence in narrative reports. Grammar: {fieldname} is a simple substitution ({individual}, {date}, {place}, {age}, {cause}, {his/her}, ...); {role=name} substitutes the name(s) of every witness on the fact whose role matches 'name' (case-insensitive) — the direct link between sentence templates and Shared Facts (see shared-facts); <...> marks a conditional block, rendered only if every placeholder inside it resolves to a non-empty value, otherwise the ENTIRE bracketed segment (including any literal punctuation inside it) is dropped; anything outside {}/<> is literal text. There are two sentence kinds — Principal sentences (from the fact-owner's own point of view) and Witness sentences (from a witness's point of view, one per role they're recorded in) — most codes work in either, some are restricted to one. Don't confuse this with Source Template *formats* (TITL/BIBL/FOOT/SHRT) — a similar-looking but separately defined mini-language used for citation formatting, more flexible than sentence templates but a distinct grammar.

title: Data Reference qualifier codes: Date qualifiers (incl. age-at)
source: FH developer-supplied source header (TN_QUALIFIER_REC g_QualArr[], qualifier codes 1-15, 32-34, 49-50) cross-checked against FH help: /help/fh8/dateformats.html, /help/fh8/sentencetemplatecodes.html; /help/fh8/understandingdatareferences.html ("Qualifiers" section)
text: Date qualifiers are a Data Reference feature (see data-references-syntax), NOT specific to Sentence Templates: any Data Reference that resolves to a date field can be qualified with a colon + qualifier name, e.g. %INDI.BIRT.DATE:YEAR% or %INDI.~SPOU>BIRT.DATE:LONG% (spouse's birth date, in Long format). Inside a Sentence Template this is written wrapped in curly brackets in addition to the percent signs — {%FACT.DATE:YEAR%} — and the standard sentence code {date:YEAR} is just sugar for the equivalent {%FACT.DATE:YEAR%} data reference over the current fact. Do not confuse this with the role-code colon syntax {role:GIVEN=roleName} (see data-reference-qualifiers-name) — same colon character, different grammar position. Canonical qualifier names (as typed after the colon): LONG (verbose, with prefixes like 'on'/'in'/'circa', affected by Preferred Standard Date Format), COMPACT (alias SHORT — abbreviated month names, still prefixed; affected by Preferred Standard Date Format), ABBREV (alias MEDIUM — further abbreviated, ranges lose the day part; affected by Preferred Standard Date Format), ABBREV2/ABBREV3 (progressively more abbreviated numeric-leaning forms; ABBREV3 is affected by Preferred SHORT Date Format specifically, not Standard), ABBREV4 (most abbreviated, e.g. bare year or year range; not affected by either preferred-format setting). Only LONG/COMPACT/ABBREV/ABBREV2/ABBREV3/ABBREV4 auto-add narrative prefixes ('on', 'in', 'circa', 'aft', 'bef', etc) — every other qualifier below returns a bare value with no prefix, so wrap it in <> with your own literal prefix text if you want one (see the sentence-templates entry's prefix/suffix note). Bare-value qualifiers, none affected by preferred-format settings except where noted, and all of which return nothing for a date range or period (simple dates only): DAY (day-of-month number), DAY_OF_WEEK (weekday name), MONTH_NUMBER (numeric month; canonical qualifier name is MONTH_NUMBER even though the internal constant is TN_QC_MONTH), MONTH_NAME, MONTH_AND_DAY (combined dd/mm or mm/dd, affected by Preferred Short Date Format), YEAR. Three qualifiers are designed to be used together for exporting a date into a spreadsheet/database column, and only make sense as a matched triple: XDATE1 (start date), XDATE2 (end date, blank for simple dates), XDATETYPE (a label: 'Date'/'Estimate'/'Approx'/'From'/'To'/'Between'/'After'/'Before'/'Phrase'/'Interpreted Phrase'). Three further qualifiers are a distinct qualifier type (IND_DATE / FAM_DATE, not the plain DATE type above) that can be applied to ANY date reference, but only produce a result for INDI/FAM dates, and only if the relevant person has a recorded birth date: AGE_AT (the age of the individual who owns the fact/data-reference chain, INDI records only), HUSBAND_AGE_AT and WIFE_AGE_AT (age of the husband/wife in a FAM fact, FAM records only) — e.g. {%FACT.DATE:AGE_AT%} inside a fact belonging to an individual gives their age at that date. Two further qualifiers, LONG_FS and COMPACT_FS, exist in the source's qualifier table but are undocumented in any FH help page found so far — likely internal-only variants used by the plain {date} code itself to build its auto-prefixed narrative text, not qualifiers a user is expected to type directly; treat as unconfirmed/internal until seen used in a real template.

title: Data Reference qualifier codes: Name qualifiers
source: FH developer-supplied source header (TN_QUALIFIER_REC g_QualArr[], qualifier codes 16-31) cross-checked against FH help: /help/fh8/nameformats.html, /help/fh8/sentencetemplatecodes.html; /help/fh8/understandingdatareferences.html ("Qualifiers" section)
text: Name qualifiers are a Data Reference feature (see data-references-syntax), NOT specific to Sentence Templates: any Data Reference that resolves to a NAME field can be qualified with a colon + qualifier name, e.g. %INDI.NAME:GIVEN_ALL% or %INDI.~SPOU>NAME:SURNAME% (spouse's surname). Inside a Sentence Template's role codes ({role:QUALIFIER=roleName}, {role(single):QUALIFIER=...}, {role(plural):QUALIFIER=...}, {other:QUALIFIER=...}, {other(single):QUALIFIER=...}, {other(plural):QUALIFIER=...} — colon goes after the code label and before the '='), the qualifier names below are used the same way, e.g. {role:GIVEN=bridesmaid}, {other(plural):SURNAME=beneficiary}. And any data reference resolving to a NAME field can use them directly, e.g. {%CUR_PRIN.FAMC>HUSB>FAMC>HUSB>NAME:SURNAME%} for a paternal grandfather's surname. Canonical qualifier names: SURNAME, FIRST (the literal first name field), GIVEN (normally the same as FIRST, but if a 'name used' override is recorded that takes precedence, and if the first name IS the surname then GIVEN is the first non-surname word instead), GIVEN_ALL (all given names, i.e. everything except the surname), MIDDLE (all given names except the first, i.e. everything except the first name and the surname), FULL (the complete name), SURNAME_FIRST (full name reordered as 'Surname, Rest'), PREFERRED (given name + surname, using the same 'given name' resolution as GIVEN), ADORNED (given+surname with name prefix prepended and name suffix appended, if recorded), PREFIXED (given+surname with prefix only), SUFFIXED (given+surname with suffix only), ADORNED_FULL / PREFIXED_FULL / SUFFIXED_FULL (same three adornment variants but built from FULL instead of given+surname), STORED (the name exactly as stored in the GEDCOM slash-delimited form, e.g. 'John /Smith/' renders literally as 'John /Smith/' — this is a debugging/raw-data qualifier, not narrative output), SOUNDEX (the surname's Soundex phonetic code, for grouping like-sounding surnames — not narrative text). All name qualifiers are valid on any record type.

title: Data Reference qualifier codes: Place and lat/long qualifiers
source: FH developer-supplied source header (TN_QUALIFIER_REC g_QualArr[], qualifier codes 35-48) cross-checked against FH help: /help/fh8/placeformats.html, /help/fh8plugins/api/functions/... (FACT.PLAC data-reference examples in sentencetemplatecodes.html); /help/fh8/understandingdatareferences.html ("Qualifiers" section)
text: Place and lat/long qualifiers are a Data Reference feature (see data-references-syntax), NOT specific to Sentence Templates: any Data Reference resolving to a PLAC field can be qualified directly, e.g. %INDI.BIRT.PLAC:SHORT%; the standard {place}/{_place} sentence codes use the 'Tidy' behaviour by default and aren't qualifiable directly by name — use a full data reference (wrapped in {%...%} inside a sentence template, e.g. {%FACT.PLAC:SHORT%}) if you need a specific one. Canonical qualifier names: SHORT (text up to the first comma only), MEDIUM (text up to the second comma, if there are two), TIDY (full place text, with duplicate/placeholder commas collapsed — e.g. 'Rothbury,, Northumberland' becomes 'Rothbury, Northumberland'), FULL (full place text, commas preserved exactly as entered — this is the default place format everywhere except the qualified codes above). Lat/long qualifiers apply to a data reference resolving to a place's coordinates, e.g. {%FACT.PLAC>LATLONG:DMS%} (the plain {%FACT.PLAC>LATLONG%} form defaults to DMS). Canonical qualifier names, each available as a combined lat+long pair or a single-axis variant: DMS (degrees/minutes/seconds, e.g. with N/S/E/W), DEGREES (decimal degrees, unsigned, with hemisphere letter), NUMERIC (signed decimal degrees, no hemisphere letter — north/east positive, south/west negative). Single-axis variants: LAT_DMS, LAT_DEGREES, LAT_NUMERIC (latitude only); LON_DMS (canonical name is LONG_DMS, not LON_DMS), LON_DEGREES (canonical name LONG_DEGREES), LON_NUMERIC (canonical name LONG_NUMERIC) (longitude only). Caution: the qualifier name string 'NUMERIC' is reused for an unrelated qualifier type — a custom/user-defined attribute's 'Numeric' edit qualifier (dataclass DC_INTEGER, valid on INDI and FAM records), used when defining how a custom attribute's value should be edited/filtered as a number rather than free text. It has nothing to do with lat/long and isn't usable in a sentence template the way the lat/long NUMERIC qualifier is — the two are disambiguated only by which field type they're attached to, not by the string itself, so don't assume every 'NUMERIC' qualifier reference means coordinates.

title: Data References: the general field-addressing syntax behind qualifiers, sentence templates, diagrams and queries
source: FH help: /help/fh8/understandingdatareferences.html ("Understanding Data References")
text: A Data Reference is FH's general expression syntax for addressing a specific field or record, written between percent signs, e.g. %INDI.NAME%. It's the mechanism underlying diagrams, websites, books, reports (including sentence templates — see sentence-templates), queries, smart folders, and some Property Box customizations — qualifier codes (see data-reference-qualifiers-date, data-reference-qualifiers-name, data-reference-qualifiers-place-latlong) are a Data Reference feature, not a Sentence-Template-only one. Grammar: a dot (.) means 'child field of' (e.g. INDI.NAME); a chevron (>) means 'follow this link to another record' (e.g. INDI.FAMC>HUSB>NAME — an individual's family-as-child, then the HUSBand in it, then that person's NAME). An index in [] after a field selects a specific instance when there's more than one: [2] (2nd instance), [last], [last-1], [<2] (2nd if present, else 1st), [preferred]/[preflast]/[prefonly] (facts only, keys off the Preferred flag), [year=1881] (a dated fact matching a year), [1+] (looping index, text schemes only, repeats for every instance from here on). By default all indices skip Rejected facts; append index flags after a comma to override — +r (include rejected), -p (exclude private), -t (exclude tentative), combinable, e.g. [3,+r] or [1+,-p,-t]. A colon + qualifier name after a field requests a specific display format for it, e.g. %INDI.NAME:SURNAME% or %INDI.BIRT.DATE:YEAR% — this is the qualifier mechanism. Shortcuts (prefixed ~) reach otherwise-hard-to-address data: ~FATH/~MOTH/~SPOU/~CHIL (usable from an Individual, e.g. INDI.~SPOU[2]>BIRT.DATE for a 2nd spouse's birth date) and ~SHAR for witnessed/shared events (chevron form INDI.~SHAR>DATE reaches the event itself; dot form INDI.~SHAR.ROLE reaches the witness link's own fields like ROLE or the _SENT sentence override). Contextual data references (no explicit starting record, meaning supplied by where the expression is used) come in two families: CUR~... ones follow a link and end in a chevron (%CUR~SPOU>%, %CUR~FAMC>%, %CUR~WITN>%), CUR_... ones reference a record directly with no chevron (%CUR_PRIN%, %CUR_PRIN2%, %CUR_FILE_ROOT%). %CUR_PRIN%/%CUR_PRIN2% and %CUR~WITN>% are the ones usable in Sentence Templates specifically (principal/second-principal/witness); the rest are diagram- or query-only. Relative data references (usable only with the GetField/GetFieldText functions, or generally within the FH plugin API) start with ~ followed by . or > instead of a tag, e.g. %~.BIRT.DATE% meaning 'relative to whatever record is implied by context'. Source Template metafields (see source-template-fields) are addressed either by tag+index (%SOUR._FIELD[2]%) or by a shortcut built from the field's 3-letter type prefix + its CODE in uppercase (%SOUR.~TX-RECORD_TITLE%); from within a citation's Footnote/Short-Footnote format, prefix with the CUR~CITN contextual reference (%CUR~CITN._FIELD%, %CUR~CITN.~TX-RECORD_TITLE%).

title: run_lua guidance: call-shape gotchas that never vary
source: server/src/runLuaTool.ts's own RUN_LUA_DESCRIPTION (moved to the corpus 2026-08-01 -- MCP clients that load tool descriptions via deferred/lazy schema-loading (e.g. ToolSearch) truncate long descriptions around ~2KB, so this content no longer lives inline past the safe zone; see docs/adr/0011-run-lua-description-truncation-workaround.md); two bullets on Date/DatePoint (GetDatePoint() doesn't exist, and preferring Data Reference qualifiers over the object chain) added 2026-08-04 from issue #51
text: A few call shapes that never vary and are easy to get wrong on a first guess — searching would have caught each of these, they're listed here only so the same mistake isn't repeated twice: - fhGetItemText(ptr, dataRef) always takes two arguments — the one-arg form fails with "Invalid number of arguments". To read an item's own value directly: fhGetItemText(itemPtr, "~"). - fhCreateItem(tag) creates a new top-level record (tag first, no parent argument); fhCreateItem(tag, parentPtr) creates a child item under an existing pointer. Either way the tag string comes first — fhCreateItem(parentPtr, tag) (parent-first) fails with "string expected, got ..." on argument #1. - fhSetValueAsText/fhSetValueAsDate/fhSetValueAsLink/etc. take exactly two arguments — (itemPtr, value) — not three; there is no dataRef parameter on the setters the way fhGetItemText has one. Set the value directly on the item pointer you just created or fetched. - fhSetValueAsLink on a CHIL item automatically creates the reciprocal FAMC on the linked Individual (and the equivalent applies to FAMS/HUSB/WIFE pairs) — manually creating your own item for "the other side" as well produces a second, stray, unlinked duplicate. This is exactly the kind of bookkeeping fhu.addFamilyAsChild/addFamilyAsSpouse exist to handle for you instead. - Descend with child:MoveToFirstChildItem(parentPtr) — the parent is the argument, not the receiver you're moving. - MoveNext() walks siblings at the same level and goes Null at the end of the record; it does not continue into the next top-level record. There is no MoveToNextSiblingItem — that name doesn't exist in FH's API. - Before iterating all records of a type with MoveToFirstRecord/MoveNext, check fhu.records(type) — a ready-made iterator — the same way you'd check fhu's mutation helpers first. fhu.allItems and fhu.indiList cover other common iteration shapes; search_fh_help for the exact signature before assuming which one fits. - Custom facts are usually not reachable by a data-reference string (~.FACT[1].TYPE and similar return empty) — walk child items with MoveToFirstChildItem/MoveNext and read each one's fhGetTag() instead. - To match, filter, or display a person's name parts (or a date/place field) via a Data Reference — e.g. "~.NAME:GIVEN_ALL", "~.NAME:SURNAME" — don't rediscover the qualifier by grepping fh-help sample scripts. search_gedcom_knowledge("name qualifiers") (and its "date qualifiers"/"place and lat/long qualifiers" siblings) returns the full canonical list of every qualifier code (data-reference-qualifiers-name/date/place-latlong), sourced from FH's own developer source header. - SEX resolves to the string "Male"/"Female", not "M"/"F" — a sex == "M" test silently matches nothing. - Family Historian resolves custom facts to their own real tags (e.g. _ATTR-REGIMENT, EVEN-ENLISTED), not a generic FACT/EVEN plus a TYPE subtag the way they'd sit in a raw GEDCOM export — walking the tree gives you the resolved tag directly. - A fact's Rejected flag always overrides its Preferred flag — a fact flagged both Rejected and Preferred is never treated as preferred. Don't read Preferred alone as "this is the one FH would display by default." - fhGetItemText/fhGetValueAsText on a Notes (or other rich-text) field returns raw FTF markup literally (e.g. a table shows up as ` apple | pear `), not clean prose — use fhGetValueAsRichText(ptr):GetPlainText() instead when you need readable text. Call search_gedcom_knowledge for the fuller FTF/domain reference (Shared Facts, Source Template fields, Sentence templates, etc.) beyond what's inlined here. - fhu.getParam, fhu.createUpdateFact, fhu.pickIndividualPrompt, fhu.yes, and fhu.stripCommas called with its optional sQuestion/sTitle/hParent arguments all open a real modal dialog inside FH and would hang a headless run_lua call — calling any of them raises a clear error instead of running. fhu.stripCommas called with just its text argument is unaffected (pure string cleanup, no dialog). fhu.saveOptions, fhu.loadOptions, and fhu.resetOptions raise the same way — they read or write a plugin-data file on disk, which this sandbox never allows. None of the eight are usable from a run_lua script in either Read-only or Read-write; don't suggest them. - fhu.createIndi (and other fhu creator functions) do NOT validate required arguments before acting — fhu.createIndi() called with zero args still creates a real, permanent blank Individual record on the spot, it just leaves sName/sSex empty. There is no dry-run and no argument-count guard to catch a bad call before it mutates the tree. Never call a creator function "just to see what error comes back" — confirm every argument via search_fh_help first. If a bad call like this does slip through, the created record generally cannot be cleaned up via fhDeleteItem from within this tool (deletions are the most heavily gated write action) — tell the user immediately so they can undo it themselves (Ctrl-Z in FH), rather than attempting further calls to fix it. - Date/DatePoint objects have no GetDatePoint() method — that name doesn't exist and errors, despite being a plausible guess from the DatePoint object's own name. Use dt:GetDatePt1() (and dt:GetDatePt2() for a date range's second point) to get a DatePoint, then DatePoint:GetYear() and its sibling methods for individual date components. - For simple date-component extraction (e.g. a birth year), prefer a Data Reference qualifier over the Date/DatePoint object chain: fhGetItemText(ptr, "~.BIRT.DATE:YEAR") returns the year directly, with no object chain and no IsNull() checks needed — search_gedcom_knowledge("date qualifiers") for the full list (data-reference-qualifiers-date). Reserve the Date/DatePoint object chain for cases that actually need it: comparison/sorting via dt:Compare()/dp:Compare(), or a full Date object.

title: run_lua guidance: fhu is already a global — don't call require
source: bridge/sandbox.lua and CONTEXT.md's Sandbox section (fhu is a proxy over the real fhUtils module, exposed as a preloaded global, never the raw module) -- added 2026-08-02 after an LLM session called require('fhUtils') per the scraped fhUtils help doc page and hit a Lua error (issue #48)
text: In this Bridge's run_lua sandbox, fhu is already a global — do not call require('fhUtils'), it returns nil here (this sandbox's _ENV never exposes require at all). Just reference fhu.<method> directly, e.g. fhu.records(type), fhu.createIndi(sName, sSex). This is bridge-sandbox-specific, not a general FH fact: an ordinary FH plugin generated by author_fh_plugin runs under FH's own trust boundary, not this sandbox, and require('fhUtils') genuinely is the correct way to get fhu there — don't apply this note to author_fh_plugin output.

title: run_lua guidance: cite every fact a source supports
source: server/src/runLuaTool.ts's own RUN_LUA_DESCRIPTION (moved to the corpus 2026-08-01 -- MCP clients that load tool descriptions via deferred/lazy schema-loading (e.g. ToolSearch) truncate long descriptions around ~2KB, so this content no longer lives inline past the safe zone; see docs/adr/0011-run-lua-description-truncation-workaround.md) and docs/adr/0006-cite-every-fact-a-source-supports.md
text: When you add tree data on the strength of a source (new or already-existing), extract everything that source supports and cite every element it touches — not just the one fact the user happened to ask about — but never write any of it without asking first. Read the source's transcription (its TEXT field, via fhGetValueAsRichText(ptr):GetPlainText()) in full, compare it against what's already on the record(s) it concerns (names, dates, places, occupations, relationships, and anything else it states), and report anything the source supports that isn't yet entered. Wait for the user's explicit go-ahead before writing any of it — do not add it silently just because the original request already authorized touching this source. To cite the source once you're adding or confirming a fact, call fhBridge.citeSource(ptrTarget, sourceIdOrTitle) rather than hand-rolling fhCreateItem("SOUR", ptrTarget) + fhSetValueAsLink yourself — it resolves the source by id or title (case-insensitive, erroring on zero or multiple matches) the same way fhBridge.createSourceFromTemplate resolves a template. ptrTarget can be an INDI/FAM record itself (FH calls this a "Whole-record" citation — for something the source establishes about the record as a whole, e.g. a birth certificate naming a parent) or a specific Fact item (for something tied to just that one event).

title: run_lua guidance: writeSessionRolledBack and FH's auto-undo
source: server/src/runLuaTool.ts's own RUN_LUA_DESCRIPTION (moved to the corpus 2026-08-01 -- MCP clients that load tool descriptions via deferred/lazy schema-loading (e.g. ToolSearch) truncate long descriptions around ~2KB, so this content no longer lives inline past the safe zone; see docs/adr/0011-run-lua-description-truncation-workaround.md) and docs/adr/0005-write-mode-errors-rethrown-for-fh-auto-undo.md
text: In a read-write Session, if a script errors after it already wrote something (e.g. it creates a record, then fails on a later step), the response carries `writeSessionRolledBack: true` and the Bridge Session ends as part of handling it — confirmed empirically (docs/adr/0005) that this is what it actually takes to give FH's own auto-undo a real chance to fire: the whole plugin has to end with the error uncaught, not just the one script. When you see this field, tell the user two things: FH should be showing its own "Plugin Error" dialog asking whether to undo the changes this plugin made — they need to click Yes there to actually undo the partial write, this tool can't do it for them — and the Bridge Session has ended, so they'll need to click Start again in the Bridge dialog before you can run another script. A write-mode script that errors before writing anything behaves exactly like Read-only: reported normally, Session stays up, no `writeSessionRolledBack`. Read-only Sessions never carry this field at all: nothing can have been written.

title: Citation quality/reliability assessment (QUAY): getting and setting via the plugin API
source: FH developer response, issue #32 (upstream question: definition of the Quay values for Source citations)
text: QUAY is a field on a Source *citation* (the link between a Fact/record and the Source it cites), not a field on the Source record itself — same citation-vs-record distinction as AUTH/TITL in data-references-syntax (reach it from a Footnote/Short Footnote format via the contextual reference %CUR~CITN.QUAY%, not %SOUR.QUAY%; see sourcetemplateformats.html's own worked example of this exact field). Despite the tag name (GEDCOM's standard QUAY certainty-assessment tag is normally a single digit 0-3), FH's plugin API exposes and stores QUAY as a human-readable, space-separated string built from up to four independent yes/no axes, each a mutually-exclusive pair of words for that axis (pick at most one word per row, never both): row 1 Unreliable/Questionable, row 2 Indirect/Direct, row 3 Secondary/Primary, row 4 Derivative/Original. Any subset of the four rows may be set (including none), e.g. "Unreliable Direct Secondary Derivative" (all four picked) or "Questionable Original" (two of four, rows 1 and 4 only) or "" (none picked). Get and set the value with the same general fhGetValueAsText/fhSetValueAsText functions used for other item values elsewhere in the API (see run-lua-guidance-call-shape-gotchas for their exact two-argument call shape) — there is no QUAY-specific getter/setter pair. fhGetValueAsText returns exactly the space-separated word string described above; fhSetValueAsText expects the same format back, and providing both words from the same row (e.g. "Unreliable Questionable") is not a valid state — the developer confirmed each row is either/or/neither, never both.

title: run_lua guidance: fhBridge.logActivity and the session's Research Note
breadcrumb: Logging activity to the session's Research Note
source: server/src/runLuaTool.ts's own RUN_LUA_DESCRIPTION (moved to the corpus 2026-08-04 -- MCP clients that load tool descriptions via deferred/lazy schema-loading (e.g. ToolSearch) truncate long descriptions around ~2KB, so this content no longer lives inline past the safe zone; see docs/adr/0011-run-lua-description-truncation-workaround.md) and docs/adr/0010-automatic-session-log-steered-from-run-lua.md, docs/adr/0012-enforce-write-then-log-via-pre-scan-and-runtime-check.md -- gap surfaced in issue #55, where a session called logActivity correctly but had no way to confirm what it did or where the result went
text: fhBridge.logActivity(ptrRecord, action, media) -- read-write only. Call it after every record-touching action in a Read-write Session (creating an Individual/Family/Source, adding or updating a Fact, anything that changes the tree), not just once at the end. action is a short free-text description, e.g. "created"; for a Fact-specific action, compose it from fhGetDisplayText(ptrFact) on the Fact's own item pointer rather than a hand-typed label -- e.g. action = "fact added " .. fhGetDisplayText(ptrFact) reads as "fact added Birth: 12 Jun 2010, London", carrying the date/place FH already knows instead of just the fact type. The first call in a Session creates one _RNOT (Research Note) record, titled "Claude session log - <timestamp>"; every later call in the same Session appends one more entry to that same note -- never create or manage the note yourself, and never call logActivity in a Read-only Session or after a script that made no writes. Each entry's record reference is a live FTF record link (RichText's AddRecordLink), not plain text, so opening the note in FH lets the user click straight through, with the label tracking the record's current display name. Where it lives: the _RNOT this produces is a completely ordinary record in the project, not a separate log file or database -- visible in FH's own UI (browse to Research Notes) once the Session ends, and readable back from a read-only script too, e.g. fhu.records("_RNOT"). Optional third argument media = {name = "...", location = "..."} (location optional): when a source discussed was backed by a physical/digital item (a photo, a certificate) the user never actually attached as media in this Session, this appends an indented "[ ] #ToDo Media to be added <name>" sub-line under the entry -- plain FTF text, not an interactive checkbox, and this project never touches the media file itself. A write made without a matching logActivity call gets rolled back, not merely warned about -- see run-lua-guidance-write-session-rolled-back for what that looks like and costs.

title: run_lua guidance: fhBridge's read-only family/detail query helpers
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua (issue #62); verified live against a real ~4000-Individual project (multiple FAMS records, custom facts, shared facts) before this entry was written; searchByName added 2026-08-04
text:
Before hand-rolling a FAMS/FAMC/HUSB/WIFE/CHIL walk (MoveTo(ptr, "~.FAMC") + MoveNext("SAME_TAG"), per run-lua-guidance-call-shape-gotchas), check fhBridge's four read-only query helpers first — available in BOTH Read-only and Read-write Sessions, unlike fhBridge.createSourceFromTemplate/citeSource/logActivity, which are Read-write only. None ever return a raw Item Pointer (jsonEncode.lua can't encode one) — every result is a plain descriptor table instead: an individual descriptor is {id, qualifiedId, name, sex}, a family descriptor is {id, qualifiedId}. The three of the four that take a pointer argument (getFamilyGroup, getAncestors, getAllDetails) also accept either a live Item Pointer or a qualified id string (e.g. "I219", the exact form every .qualifiedId field already returns) anywhere they take that argument — so a result from one call can be fed straight into the next without resolving it to a pointer by hand first, e.g. fhBridge.getAllDetails(group[1].individual.qualifiedId). searchByName is the odd one out: it takes no pointer at all, since it searches across every Individual in the project rather than working from one.

fhBridge.getFamilyGroup(indiPtr, type) — type is one of "all" (default), "parents", "siblings", "spouses". Walks every FAMC/FAMS record the Individual belongs to, not just the first (someone married more than once has multiple FAMS records; someone with more than one recorded family-as-child has multiple FAMC). Returns an array of {relationship, individual, family}: relationship is "father"/"mother" (read off the FAMC record's HUSB/WIFE link itself, not the parent's own SEX field), "sibling", or "spouse"; family identifies which FAMC/FAMS record the relationship came through, so two entries with different .family.id are half-siblings (or a different marriage), not full siblings (or the same marriage). Never includes indiPtr itself, and dedupes by relationship+id.

fhBridge.getAncestors(indiPtr, maxGenerations) — breadth-first walk up every FAMC record; generation 1 is indiPtr's own parents, generation 2 their parents, and so on. maxGenerations is optional (omit/nil for unlimited, bounded by the tree's own depth and watchdog.lua's instruction budget). Returns an array of {generation, line, individual, family}: line is an array of "father"/"mother" steps from indiPtr down to that ancestor (e.g. {"mother","father"} is the maternal grandfather) — deliberately not resolved to an English title like "grandfather", build that yourself from generation+line if you need it. Dedupes by record id (pedigree collapse): an ancestor reachable via more than one path is reported once, at its shallowest generation.

fhBridge.getAllDetails(ptr) — works on any item pointer, not just a top-level record (a Fact item works too). Recursively describes ptr and every child/subfield beneath it as one plain tree: {tag, id/qualifiedId (record items only), value (items that store one — fhGetValueType is "" for records/flags/complex container items like BIRT itself), link (link-classed items only — a plain descriptor of the linked record: {tag, id, qualifiedId, text}, NOT the target's own fields, since following FAMS/FAMC/HUSB/WIFE/CHIL back out would walk the whole connected tree and could cycle forever), children}. richtext fields go through GetPlainText() (see run-lua-get-plain-text-from-richtext), not raw FTF markup.

getFamilyGroup and getAncestors both raise a clear error if the resolved pointer/qualified id isn't an INDI record (e.g. passing a family's "F13" by mistake) — getAllDetails accepts any record type's qualified id, matching its "any record pointer" contract.

fhBridge.searchByName(forename, surname) — finds every Individual whose given name(s) contain forename and whose surname contains surname, matched case-insensitively as substrings, not exact/whole-word (searchByName("Robert", "Taubman") also matches "Robert Henry TAUBMAN"). Either argument may be omitted or "" to skip filtering on that part of the name; passing neither raises an error rather than silently scanning every Individual in the project. Matches against the NAME field's GIVEN_ALL/SURNAME Data Reference qualifiers (see data-reference-qualifiers-name), not the raw stored NAME text or fhIndGetName's display string, so it matches consistently regardless of how a given record orders/prefixes its name parts. Returns an array of individual descriptors, the same shape as the other three helpers' .individual field, in FH's own record order (creation order, not sorted alphabetically) — not deduped or ranked by relevance, since there's no relationship path to dedupe against the way getFamilyGroup/getAncestors have.
